messages:
liz: Quick RFC follow-up — we should decide whether the quota credit snapshotting approach is append-only oplog + periodic full snapshots, or streaming checkpoints with diff compaction. tradeoffs: replay speed vs storage + GC complexity.

sam: +1 on discussing. core goal for me: make post-failover reconciliation fast (<250ms) for hot tenants. replaying thousands of ops is not acceptable.

akira: can we do a hybrid? keep a small rolling snapshot every minute + an oplog of deltas. then playback is snapshot + tail. sounds similar to what DBs do though.

jon: hybrid seems sensible. question: where do we store snapshots? s3-style cold + memcached hot? snapshots must be single-file per-epoch for atomicity.

liz: exactly. envisioned: epoch-id -> snapshot blob in object store, and a short-lived write-ahead log in fast kv for deltas. on failover, coordinator fetches latest snapshot and applies oplog since snapshot_ts.

sam: implementation detail: oplog entries must be idempotent and include monotonic sequence numbers + per-tenant sequence base. otherwise we risk double-apply when partial replay happens.

akira: agreed. also include a simple crc/hash at snapshot footer and on oplog batches so we detect mismatch early and fall back to full rebuild.

jon: tradeoffs again: full snapshots every minute increase object store ops and size. but reduces replay time. we could adaptive-sample by tenant QPS: hot tenants get 10s snapshots, cold ones 5m.

liz: love that — adaptive snapshot cadence by QPS. need guardrails so snapshot churn doesn't flood storage. maybe a daily cap per tenant or global budget.

sam: about fairness scheduling integration — snapshots must capture tenant queues and leaky-bucket state (tokens, bucket timestamp). otherwise fair scheduler can't reconstruct in-flight credits.

akira: can we compress bucket state? pack using base-timestamp + token-count + recent-burst-window counter. keeps snapshot small.

jon: also need a reconciliation mode for cross-region handoff. if primary loses network, standby might be slightly behind; we should support a "soft-probation" that enforces conservative limits for 30s while we rehydrate exact state. avoids overserving during uncertain windows.

liz: good call. add a probation bucket: new region starts with min(local-estimate, snapshot-estimate) and ramps up based on confirmed acked ops.

sam: abuse prevention note: we should record fuzzy per-tenant anomaly markers in snapshot (e.g., recent-peak-rate, abnormal-pattern-bitset) so on failover we don't immediately treat a spike as normal.

akira: flagging there are privacy considerations for storing request fingerprints. keep it aggregated (counts/histograms), no raw prompts.

jon: ops: need a migration path from current token-mux design. propose we implement snapshotting as an optional sidecar; rollout with canary tenants and metric gating.

liz: action items: 1) akira to draft the snapshot schema (1 pager) — include epoch-id, base-timestamp, bucket-states, anomaly-aggregates, crc. 2) sam to prototype oplog format + idempotency tokens. 3) jon to sketch storage budget and adaptive cadence heuristics. 4) ops: schedule small canary with infra-bot to run reconciliation test.

infra-bot: scheduled test job quota-reconciler/canary-001 for 2026-05-12T14:00Z (run id: canary-001). See https://ci.internal/recon/canary-001

sam: quick open question — do we want strong ordering across all token shards, or per-tenant ordering only? strong global ordering is costly.

akira: per-tenant ordering is sufficient for fairness and simpler. global ordering only needed for cross-tenant billing invariants, which we can reconcile asynchronously.

liz: agreed: per-tenant sequencing + global eventual accounting works. we'll note billing invariants in the RFC appendix.

jon: one more: compaction policy for oplog — when snapshot_ts >= op_ts, delete older oplogs. but keep last N oplogs for quick rollback. choose N based on snapshot cadence.

liz: ok. I'll fold these notes into the RFC follow-up doc and tag the design PR. thanks all. :thanks:
